content.user_title: Process PDFs with Text, Tables, and Forms
content.value_statement: PDF workflows often require text extraction, table capture, form filling, splitting, and merging. This skill provides practical Python patterns for common PDF processing tasks.
actual_capabilities: Extract text from individual pages or full documents with pdfplumber.
Extract detected tables from PDFs and write them to CSV.
Fill and flatten PDF form fields with pypdf examples.
Merge several PDF files into one document.
Split selected page ranges into a new PDF.
Handle empty or scanned pages with basic error checks.
limitations: Examples assume the required Python packages are installed.
OCR guidance depends on external tesseract and poppler tools.
Form filling requires accurate field names from the source PDF.
Scanned PDFs may need OCR before text or table extraction.

use_cases.title: Extract Report Data
use_cases.description: Analysts can pull text and tables from PDF reports for review or spreadsheet work.

use_cases.title: Prepare Form Packets
use_cases.description: Office staff can inspect fields, fill values, and flatten completed PDF forms.

use_cases.title: Reorganize Document Sets
use_cases.description: Legal or finance users can merge related files or split selected pages for distribution.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Text From a PDF
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pdf-processing skill to extract readable text from document.pdf and summarize any pages that return no text.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Tables to CSV
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to extract tables from report.pdf and prepare a CSV output plan with field cleanup notes.

prompt_templates.title: Fill and Flatten a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect form.pdf fields, map my provided values to field names, fill the PDF, and flatten the result.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Batch PDF Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a batch process that extracts text, exports tables, splits selected pages, and reports processing errors.

output_examples.input: Extract text from a 20-page policy PDF.
output_examples.output: A page-by-page extraction summary with notes for pages that contain no selectable text.

output_examples.input: Fill a client intake form and make the fields non-editable.
output_examples.output: A completed form workflow that maps field names, validates required values, and produces a flattened PDF.

output_examples.input: Merge monthly invoice PDFs and export one selected page range.
output_examples.output: A document assembly plan with one merged PDF and a separate file for the requested page range.

best_practices: Work on copies of source PDFs before writing outputs.
Inspect PDF form field names before mapping user data.
Test extraction on a small page range before batch processing.
anti_patterns: Running examples on original documents without backups.
Assuming scanned pages contain selectable text.
Filling forms before validating required values and field names.

faq.question: Which libraries does this skill use?
faq.answer: It shows examples with pdfplumber, pypdf, pdf2image, and pytesseract.

faq.question: Can it process scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: It notes OCR packages for scanned PDFs, but text extraction may require tesseract and poppler.

faq.question: Does it modify original PDFs?
faq.answer: The examples write new output files. The guide recommends keeping originals and working on copies.

faq.question: Can it fill PDF forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes field inspection, form value updates, validation, and flattening examples.

faq.question: Can it merge and split PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for merging multiple PDFs and extracting selected page ranges.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows use local PDF files and local output files.
